management_notes: CFO transition: Eric Tsung (CPA, CGA, 20+ years corporate finance/accounting experience) appointed effective November 1, 2026 — announced November 13, 2026. This partially addresses the management continuity uncertainty flagged in prior runs; Tsung brings stronger disclosed credentials than the prior CFO. CEO remains Conan McIntyre (confirmed since the May 2026 leadership restructuring in which Paul Sobie stepped down to focus on exploration). The dual-name disclosure issue from the March→May 2026 period appears resolved with this stabilised leadership team. However, the management team as a whole still lacks a proven record of advancing a junior to resource stage and creating durable shareholder value: share price remains at multi-cent levels with ~317M shares outstanding. No insider-buying signals found. CFO appointment is a positive step but insufficient to raise the score from 2.
geology_notes: Black Raven Antimony-Gold Property (~60 km northwest of Gander, NL) is a past-producing site. Spring 2026 final assays (released August 28, 2026) confirmed 19.23% Sb over 1.40 m at Frost Cove North with structural continuity over 800 m; a copper-silver prospect (0.78% Cu, 61.2 g/t Ag over 6.22 m) was delineated alongside 20 gold-silver-molybdenum-lead-zinc veins in a 150 m wide swarm at Pomley Cove Pond. The Fall 2026 drill program has now commenced at Frost Cove — a TipRanks announcement (undated but appearing post-November 2026) is titled 'Churchill Resources Launches Fall Exploration at Frost Cove Antimony Mine,' and MiningFeeds carries a headline 'Massive Stibnite Seams Uncovered as Churchill Resources Expands Drilling at Frost Cove Antimony Mine.' Specific grades and intervals from the fall program are not yet available in published sources as of this run. Historical high-grade grab samples (up to 35.1% Sb, 14.4 g/t Au) remain selective. Golden Baie (100% option, TSXV-approved March 2026) adds a second antimony-gold land package; no drill program announced there yet. No NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate exists. Score remains 3: strong grade signals and an active fall program that appears to be producing new discovery-grade results, but no defined resource underpins the geology.
capital_notes: 316,681,940 shares issued and outstanding; 342,756,940 fully diluted — approximately 8.2% overhang (2,625,000 warrants + 23,450,000 options). The warrant tranche is small and dilution impact modest. Option book (~7.4% of outstanding) is material — strike prices and expiries were not extractable from the Q1 2026 MD&A source (extracted 2026-05-14). No flow-through tranches detected in the extraction. No new financing news found in this run. At current price levels any equity financing would be heavily dilutive. Cap structure is mid-range for a micro-cap TSXV explorer at this stage. Data drawn from Q1 2026 MD&A extraction; no updated filing available in the extraction cache.
catalyst_notes: Fall 2026 drill program is now active at Frost Cove, Black Raven — a material upgrade over the prior run's status of 'no confirmed start.' The fall program was flagged in the August 28 release as targeting extensions of holes PC26-03 and PC26-16 across the principal vein system, followed by systematic delineation along strike. Headlines suggest 'massive stibnite seams' have been uncovered in the fall program, though quantitative assay results are not yet published. Additional near-term catalysts: (1) fall program assay results at Black Raven — expected 4–8 weeks after drilling completion; (2) maiden drill announcement at Golden Baie; (3) maiden resource estimate once sufficient data accumulate; (4) antimony's critical mineral designation across the US, Canada, and EU continues to drive strategic attention. The active fall program and apparent new discovery headline justify holding catalyst at 3; a confirmed high-grade assay release from the fall program would push this to 4.
acquisition_notes: No NI 43-101 resource in place; P/NAV comparison is not possible; NAV per share is null. The strategic acquisition case is real — antimony is on US, Canadian, and EU critical minerals lists due to its use in munitions, flame retardants, and battery technology — and the fall 2026 program's apparent stibnite seam discovery may strengthen the technical case for acquirer interest. However, acquirers require a resource estimate before valuing a property. At its current market cap, entry cost is low, but no near-term acquisition event is likely absent a resource. Score remains 2.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (TSXV: CRI) is a micro-cap antimony-gold explorer in Newfoundland with two properties (Black Raven, Golden Baie) hosting genuinely exceptional drill grades — 19.23% Sb over 1.40 m in Spring 2026 stands out against virtually any peer. Antimony's critical mineral designation adds strategic weight. Two material updates since the November 18, 2026 run: (1) Eric Tsung (CPA/CGA, 20+ years experience) was appointed CFO effective November 1, 2026 — the first formal CFO credential disclosure in recent history and a partial response to the management continuity concerns flagged in prior runs; (2) the Fall 2026 drill program at Frost Cove has launched, with a headline suggesting 'massive stibnite seams' have been uncovered — specific assay results are not yet published. The core problem remains pre-resource stage: no NI 43-101 estimate, no formal mine plan, no resource-to-acquisition bridge. The share count is high at 317M. Key watch triggers: (1) fall program assay release — if grades match or exceed the Spring 2026 19.23% Sb intercept, this becomes a BUY candidate; (2) maiden resource estimate; (3) formal drill announcement at Golden Baie; (4) strategic partnership or offtake driven by antimony supply-chain urgency. Cap-table fields drawn from Q1 2026 MD&A extraction (extracted 2026-05-14); strike/expiry detail on warrants and options was not available. No resource/reserve data available from the August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report extraction.
